one_liner: Apache MXNet: archived C++ deep learning framework; 2020 ResNet-50 runs on V100 had it slightly ahead of PyTorch and TensorFlow.
what_it_does: General deep learning framework with a C++ core (libmxnet), a C API, and front ends for Python (Gluon imperative API, NumPy-style mx.np, legacy Module/Symbol), R, Julia, Scala, Clojure, Perl and an optional C++ package. Gluon blocks run eagerly and can be turned into a static graph with hybridize(). Data-parallel training uses its own KVStore (ps-lite), Horovod or BytePS. It replaces TensorFlow or PyTorch only by porting your training code to it. It does not accept their models or scripts directly.
how_it_is_fast: Every operator is pushed to an asynchronous dependency engine (ThreadedEnginePerDevice by default). The engine orders work by read/write dependencies on variables, so compute, host-device copies and gradient communication overlap. Hybridized graphs get memory planning, bulk execution of up to MXNET_EXEC_BULK_EXEC_MAX_NODE_TRAIN nodes per engine op to close kernel-launch gaps, and runtime-compiled pointwise fusion (MXNET_USE_FUSION, Gluon only with static_alloc=True). Optimizer updates can be aggregated across many weights per call (MXNET_OPTIMIZER_AGGREGATION_SIZE). Convolutions and GEMMs come from cuDNN (autotuned by default) and cuBLAS, or from oneDNN on CPU. The fastest DLPerf rows ran NVIDIA's NGC build and DeepLearningExamples script, which added DALI GPU decoding, Horovod with a 64 MB fusion buffer and tuned engine variables. Its fp16 runs also used NHWC layouts with fused BatchNorm-ReLU and BatchNorm-add-ReLU kernels.
when_to_use: Maintaining or reproducing existing MXNet/Gluon code (GluonCV, GluonNLP, 2017-2022 papers, older AWS pipelines) when a port to another framework is not worth it.

Data-parallel CNN training on V100-era GPUs with the NGC MXNet container, DALI and Horovod. DLPerf measured NGC MXNet at 11331.93 img/s FP32 and 30713.68 img/s fp16 on 32 V100s, ahead of NGC PyTorch and NGC TensorFlow 1.x.
Single-GPU FP32 ResNet-50 training on V100 with upstream 1.6.0 and gluon-cv: 384.19 img/s against 348.62 for PyTorch 1.6.0 and 321.80 for TensorFlow 2.3.
Serving an existing MXNet model from a non-Python language binding (Scala, Clojure, Perl, R, Julia, C API) on CPU (x86-64 or aarch64 wheels) or on CUDA 11.x GPUs.
when_not_to_use: Any new project. The repository was archived (read-only) on 2023-11-17, the project was retired to the Apache Attic, the last release is 1.9.1 (May 2022), and fixes are no longer made.
Current GPUs and toolchains. The newest prebuilt GPU wheel is mxnet-cu117 1.9.1 (CUDA 11.7, x86-64 only). There are no CUDA 12 wheels, and the 1.9.1 wheel pins numpy<2.0.

Mixed-precision training on the upstream gluon-cv path. On 32 V100s DLPerf measured 10565.55 img/s, against 19314.31 for TensorFlow 2.3 and 22551.16 for NGC PyTorch. At 8 GPUs it scaled only 3.49x over 1 GPU.

Multi-threaded inference through Gluon. CachedOp and the graph executor are documented as not thread safe. The thread-safe CachedOp C API supports only a tested model list, one model per process, dense storage and no dynamic shapes.

Large-scale BERT or transformer work. DLPerf's MXNet BERT rows ran without gradient clipping and still trailed OneFlow run the same way. Modern attention kernels (FlashAttention-class) and compiler stacks are not integrated.

integration.form: shared lib (libmxnet.so) behind a C API, shipped as pip wheels (mxnet, mxnet-cuXX); optional C++ package (USE_CPP_PACKAGE, off by default)
integration.dependencies: GPU builds: CUDA, cuDNN, optionally NCCL and cuTENSOR. CPU: a BLAS (OpenBLAS or MKL), oneDNN, OpenMP, optionally OpenCV. Python wheel 1.9.1: numpy (>1.16.0,<2.0.0), requests, graphviz (<0.9.0). Horovod or BytePS for multi-node training.
integration.min_toolchain: v1.x branch (1.9.1 releases): CMake 3.13 and C++11 (C++14 in some configurations). master branch (unreleased 2.0): C++17, GCC 7 or newer, CMake 3.13, CUDA C++14.
integration.platforms: PyPI wheels: Linux x86-64 and aarch64 (1.9.x), macOS x86-64 CPU, Windows x86-64 up to 1.7.0.post2. GPU wheels are NVIDIA CUDA only, up to CUDA 11.7, x86-64.
integration.thread_safety: The dependency engine is thread safe (except WaitToRead in a spawned thread). The graph executor and Gluon CachedOp are not. A thread-safe CachedOp (MXCreateCachedOp with thread_safe=true) exists for inference with the documented limitations.

gotchas: Harness flaw: the exact script behind the upstream MXNet ResNet-50 rows is not published. At the pinned gluon-cv commit f9a8a284b8, train_horovod.py has its per-batch 'Speed: ... samples/sec' log line commented out and logs 'Epoch[0] Batch[N] Loss[...]' lines instead. DLPerf's extract_mxnet_logs.py looks for 'Speed:' on every 'Epoch[0] Batch[' line (IndexError on the Loss line) and needs exactly 120 such lines. DLPerf's runner.sh, however, runs a full epoch with no 120-iteration stop, so OneFlow used a locally modified script that is not in Oneflow-Inc/DLPerf.

The upstream rows labelled AMP are pure fp16, not AMP: gluon-cv casts the whole net with net.cast('float16') and uses multi-precision NAG. The data path is a CPU gluon DataLoader with Python augmentation (8 decode workers per GPU process on a 2x12-core Xeon Gold 5118 node). The 3.49x 8-GPU scaling points to an input-bound script rather than slow framework code, but DLPerf did not measure the cause.

Upstream and NGC MXNet are not the same configuration. gluon-cv calls hybridize() without static_alloc, so Gluon pointwise fusion is off. The NGC run sets tuned engine and Horovod variables, uses DALI GPU decoding (DLPerf patched dali.py to run it in the 20.03 container), and for fp16 uses NHWC with fused BatchNorm kernels. Treat 'MXNet beats PyTorch at 32 GPUs' as an NVIDIA-container result.

The default branch (master) is the never-released 2.0 line (2.0.0b1 on PyPI, March 2022), with NumPy-style mx.np semantics. Stable 1.x releases come from the v1.x branch, and open issue #20675 reports MXNet 2.0 up to 10x slower than 1.x on Windows.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick MXNet over PyTorch only when the code or model already exists in MXNet, or for V100-era CNN training in NVIDIA's NGC MXNet container. Upstream PyTorch matched or beat upstream MXNet from 8 GPUs up in DLPerf, and PyTorch is maintained. For a C++-first training framework, look at Flashlight. For C++ inference of an exported model, OpenVINO or CTranslate2 are maintained alternatives.
verified_claims_summary: OneFlow's DLPerf v1.0 (Oct 2020) measured ResNet-50 training throughput on 4 nodes of 8x V100-SXM2-16GB (Xeon Gold 5118, CUDA 10.2, cuDNN 7.6.5). The median of 5 to 7 runs, iterations 21-120, was used. Upstream MXNet 1.6.0 with gluon-cv and Horovod did 384.19 img/s on 1 GPU at FP32 bsz 128, against PyTorch 1.6.0 348.62 and TensorFlow 2.3 321.80. Upstream MXNet trailed PyTorch at 8 and 32 GPUs. NVIDIA's NGC MXNet 20.03 container led NGC PyTorch and TensorFlow 1.x at every GPU count in FP32 and fp16. All frameworks use the same cuDNN and cuBLAS kernels, so the gaps measure framework overhead, input pipeline and communication.
status_note: Abandoned: last commit 2023-01-26, last release 1.9.1 (May 2022), repository archived 2023-11-17 and project retired to the Apache Attic (retired September 2023, move completed February 2024 according to a search snippet of attic.apache.org). Apache-2.0 and usable for legacy code, but with no CUDA 12 or NumPy 2 support and no further fixes.
